CLI for Tines

Options:

Commands:

  projects          Manage projects

Usage: tines issues artifacts attach [options] <ref> <name> [source]

Attach content to a named artifact slot — <source> is typed by the gate, flags
override (creates it, or appends a version)

Options:
  -f, --file <path>         upload a file (MIME sniffed from the extension)
  --folder <dir>            snapshot a directory tree as one version (collect
                            locally, attach once; MIME per file sniffed)
  -t, --text <md|@file>     inline text document: inline Markdown or @file
  --link <url>              link: the URL to attach
  --pr <spec>               PR reference: owner/repo#N or a GitHub PR URL
  --content-type <mime>     declared MIME type (with --file or --text)
  --filename <name>         display filename (with --text; defaults to
                            <name>.md)
  --title <title>           display title (with --link)
  -d, --description <text>  artifact description, shown in lists and launch
                            prompts
  --ignore-gates            attach this type even when a transition requirement
                            rejects it (skips inference and the pre-flight
                            checks)
  -u, --url <url>           base URL of the Tines API (or set TINES_API_URL, or
                            run `tines login`; default
                            https://tines.tbuckley.dev)
  --api-key <key>           API key (or set TINES_API_KEY, or run `tines login`)
  --json                    output the raw JSON response
  -h, --help                display help for command

Source:
  Prefer the positional form: it is what a gated slot's own hint prints
  ("fix:" on `tines issues show`, and the launch prompt's Requires: line).
  A positional <source> is typed by the slot's gate when this issue has one:
  a text gate reads the path as the document (the gate's content type wins over
  the extension), a file gate uploads its bytes, a folder gate walks it, and a
  link/pr gate takes a URL or owner/repo#N. "-" reads stdin under a text or
  file gate.

  With no gate, the shape alone decides: a directory is a folder, an http(s)
  URL is a link (a GitHub PR URL is a pr), owner/repo#N is a pr, and anything
  else is a file — a .md path included. Inline text is never inferred: pass it
  with --text.

  Flags still override, and are refused before any network write when no
  available transition's requirement for the slot could ever accept what they
  would create. --ignore-gates attaches it anyway. Prefix a source starting
  with "-" with "--".
